about.title: Westmorland Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Westmorland is a small place — roughly 2,267 residents in Imperial County — and most of its daily business happens along a handful of blocks near W Main Street, 6th Street and 8th Street. A fall there is rarely dramatic in the moment. Someone slips on a wet entry at a market, catches a heel on broken pavement outside a shop, or misses a step in a poorly lit stairwell, and the pain arrives later. California law gives you a path forward when that happens, but it puts a burden on you: showing the property owner knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have, and did nothing to fix it or warn you. That is why what you do in the first days matters so much. Photographs of the spot, the names of anyone who saw you fall, and a prompt request that the business keep its surveillance footage can carry a case in a town where witnesses are few. LawProactive is free, and the independent attorneys we connect you with work on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Use LawProactive After a Fall in Westmorland

items.title: Attorneys who understand the notice requirement
items.desc: California asks you to show the owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to build that proof through inspection logs, maintenance records, and witness accounts.

items.title: Fast action on evidence that disappears
items.desc: Surveillance video is often overwritten within days, and a spill is mopped up within minutes. Getting connected quickly means a preservation letter can go out before that footage is gone.

items.title: Clear guidance on deadlines and shared fault
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but claims against a city or county entity must be started far sooner. And because the state uses pure comparative fault, being partly to blame reduces a recovery rather than erasing it — an attorney can walk you through what that means for your situation.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk in Westmorland. Is the city responsible or the business next to it?
items.answer: It depends on who owns and controls that stretch of pavement, and the answer is not always obvious from the street. If a public entity is involved, California requires a written government claim within a much shorter window than the usual two years, so the timing matters. An attorney can look at the property records and tell you which deadline applies before it slips by.

items.question: The store says I was not paying attention. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California follows pure comparative fault, which means a jury can assign you a share of responsibility and still hold the property owner accountable for its share. Your compensation would be reduced by your percentage, not eliminated. Documenting the hazard well — photos, lighting conditions, absence of warning signs — helps keep that percentage honest.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall at a Westmorland business?
items.answer: Get medical attention first, even if you think you can walk it off, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Then photograph the exact spot, note the time and conditions, and ask for an incident report from the manager. Request in writing that any camera footage be kept; in a small town with few passersby, that video may be the strongest independent account of what happened.
